messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT — Inference error rate spike observed in us-west-2a (AZ az1a). Metrics: request errors ↑, KV cache miss ↑, NLB target unhealthy count rising. Possible egress/ENI drops. Paging oncall.

lena-oncall: on it. taking pager. pulling dashboards now. what's the scope? :eyes:

sre-jordan: I'm seeing bursts of ENI tx drops and socket econnreset on a subset of hosts in az1a. NLB target unhealthy went from 2->28 in 7m. CloudWatch link: https://cw.aws/... (truncated)

olivia-runtime: model servers p50/p99 jumped. KV cache miss rate spiked 4x — we may be losing connections to cache or facing KV cache regen thrash. Logs: `kvcache: regen started for shard-7`

ram-infra: AWS health events show network path flaps in us-west-2a around 06:14 UTC. Also seeing increased resolver RTTs (~10->60ms). suspect egress path.

lena-oncall: plan: 1) adjust traffic weights to steer away from az1a, 2) drain instances in az1a group, 3) enable cross-region fallback for critical_reserved customers, 4) open customer comms. executing step 1 now.

lena-oncall: running:
```
rbctl traffic steer set --az az1a --weight 0.15 --reason "egress queue pressure"
```

sre-jordan: noted. starting drain on target group tg-az1a-inference. `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn ... --targets Id=...` will stagger 20s.

eng-max: toggled kvcache regen backoff and bumped connection pool keepalive to 45s to reduce churn. pushing config to az1a hosts now.

olivia-runtime: temporary param to reduce batch size for degraded mode: `max_batch_tokens: 512 -> 256` to keep latency bounded if we can't fully shift traffic.

product-ash: quick customer impact: our telemetry shows ~18 customers with elevated latency; two customers reporting failed requests (session ids attached in private). preparing comms for those with SLA risk.

support-bot: created incident INC-2026-789 and posted initial status to status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2026-789 :clipboard:

lena-oncall: handoff: @ram-infra please keep the traffic steering on while we monitor for 10m. escalate to infra-eng if errors don't reduce.

ram-infra: ack. holding weight at 0.15 for now. monitoring NLB healthy host counts.

sre-jordan: after drain started healthy host count increased slightly but errors still at 1.9%. suspect ephemeral queue pressure on proxies — hitting connection queues on proxy layer.

olivia-runtime: started a lightweight restart of proxy workers on 3 hosts (staggered). curl health check before/after:
```
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:9000/health || echo "unhealthy"
```

eng-max: traffic shift executed at 06:22 UTC. dashboards: p50 latency dropped from 220ms->160ms, error rate from 2.8%->1.1%. still above baseline.

sre-jordan: metrics snapshot: throughput -18%, p50 120ms->160ms, p99 540ms->880ms, errors 0.3%->1.1%. kvcache miss rate down but still elevated.

lena-oncall: good progress. next: continue drains, keep kbcache backoff in place, if errors <0.5% in 15m we'll keep gradual restore. otherwise continue cross-region shift.

support-bot: sent comms to impacted customers and opened a private status for enterprise customers.

eng-max: note — enabling cross-region fallback for reserved-critical customers now (eu-west-1) to avoid cold-starts set `preferred_region: eu-west-1` for those tenants.

incidents-bot: automatic note: traffic steering completed, 12/15 targets drained successfully, remaining 3 draining.

product-ash: recommend notifying sales for accounts that may request postmortem.

lena-oncall: handing monitoring to @sre-maria for night watch at 08:00 UTC. I'll be reachable if it spins back up. adding follow-up todo: deep root-cause with infra and AWS support.

sre-maria: Taking handoff. will watch dashboards and escalate if >0.8% errors or p99>800ms. please add me to the incident ticket for notes.

lena-oncall: done. thanks team :heart:

incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-789 updated: status -> monitoring. last action: traffic steer and instance drain. timeline link: https://internal/incidents/INC-2026-789
